newsitem.title: UK: UK's SFA fines stockbroker Quilter for failings.
newsitem.headline: UK's SFA fines stockbroker Quilter for failings.

text.p: British financial regulator the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) on Thursday fined stockbroking firm Quilter & Co 65,000 pounds ($106,000) for failings in its dividends department and back office.
SFA said in a statement it had reprimanded the firm, which had agreed to pay its costs of 25,000 pounds, for the internal control and compliance failings.

The watchdog said that during March 1995, a probationary employee at Quilter, a London-based stockbroking firm, "committed offences of false accounting which resulted in a loss to the firm of approximately 38,000 pounds ($62,100) ".

Quilter discovered the offences and notified the SFA in November 1995. This led to an SFA investigation which identified "a number of internal control and compliance failings within the firm's dividend department" between February 1992 and December 1995.

SFA said that in settling the matter, it had taken into account that during much of the period Quilter had suffered severe operational difficulties as a result of bomb damage to its premises in April 1992 and May 1993 which forced it into temporary accomodation for two years.

It had also factored in that there was no reason to believe any client had suffered losses, the firm had co-operated fully with it and had a previously clean record with the regulator. ($ = 0.611 British Pounds)
